title: Mutual Release of Claims
summary: Two parties settle a dispute or end a relationship by releasing each other from claims.
useWhen: Both sides want to close out a dispute, a terminated contract or a business relationship so neither can sue the other later over it.
watchOuts: A release generally covers only claims that exist when it is signed, not future claims.

Some rights cannot be released, for example certain wage claims, workers' compensation and unemployment benefits. Releases of federal age-discrimination claims must meet Older Workers Benefit Protection Act requirements, including 21 days to consider and 7 days to revoke.
California requires an express waiver of Civil Code §1542 to release unknown claims. Other states have similar rules. The template adds the waiver when California law is chosen.
Employment settlements: federal law limits confidentiality and non-disparagement terms in some situations, for example sexual harassment claims under the Speak Out Act.
Settlement payments may have tax consequences and reporting requirements.

variables.label: First party: full legal name
variables.help: Full legal name of the person, or the exact registered name of the company.

variables.label: Second party: full legal name
variables.help: Full legal name of the person, or the exact registered name of the company.

variables.label: What is being released
variables.help: Describe the dispute, contract or relationship, e.g. 'all claims arising from the website development agreement dated June 1, 2025'.

variables.label: Other promises (optional)
variables.help: E.g. return of property, deleting files, withdrawing reviews.

variables.label: Keep settlement terms confidential?
variables.help: Parties agree not to disclose the terms.

variables.label: Governing law (state)
variables.help: Two-letter code of the state whose law governs this agreement. Usually where the parties or the work are located.

sections.title: 1. Parties and background
sections.body:
**First party:** {{party_a_name}}, {{party_a_address}} ({{party_a_email}})

**Second party:** {{party_b_name}}, {{party_b_address}} ({{party_b_email}})

Effective {{effective_date}}. The parties want to fully resolve the following matter without any admission of fault: {{dispute}} (the "Matter").

sections.title: 2. Payment
sections.body: The {{payer}} will pay {{payment_amount}} to the other party by {{payment_due}}. The releases below take effect when that payment is received.

sections.title: 4. Mutual release
sections.body: Each party, for itself and its owners, affiliates, successors, heirs and assigns, releases the other party and its owners, officers, employees, agents, affiliates, successors and assigns from all claims, demands, damages and causes of action, known or unknown, that arise out of or relate to the Matter and that exist up to the effective date. This release does not cover (a) obligations created by this agreement, (b) claims that cannot be released as a matter of law, or (c) claims arising after the effective date.

sections.title: 5. Waiver of California Civil Code §1542
sections.body: Each party expressly waives the protection of California Civil Code §1542, which says: "A general release does not extend to claims that the creditor or releasing party does not know or suspect to exist in his or her favor at the time of executing the release and that, if known by him or her, would have materially affected his or her settlement with the debtor or released party." Initials: First party [[initial:partyA]]  Second party [[initial:partyB]]

sections.title: 6. No admission
sections.body: This agreement is a compromise. It is not an admission of liability or wrongdoing by anyone.

sections.title: 7. No claims filed
sections.body: Each party confirms it has not assigned any released claim to anyone else, and will not sue the other on a released claim. Nothing here prevents a party from filing a charge with, or participating in an investigation by, a government agency, although a party waives any right to recover money from the released claims where the law allows such a waiver.

sections.title: 8. Confidentiality
sections.body: The parties will keep the terms of this agreement confidential, except as required by law, for tax or legal advice, or to enforce it. This does not limit any right to speak about matters the law protects, such as reporting unlawful conduct to the government.

sections.title: 9. Advice of counsel
sections.body: Each party has read this agreement, understands it, had the chance to consult a lawyer, and signs voluntarily.

sections.title: 10. General terms
sections.body:
- **Whole agreement.** This document (with any attachments named in it) is the parties' entire agreement on its subject and replaces earlier discussions and drafts.
- **Changes.** It can only be changed in a writing signed by all parties.
- **Severability.** If a court finds any part unenforceable, that part is limited to the minimum extent needed and the rest stays in effect.
- **No waiver.** Not enforcing a term once is not a waiver of it later.
- **Notices.** Notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, by a recognized courier, by certified mail, or by email to the addresses in this document (or a later address a party gives in writing). Email notice is effective when sent unless the sender receives a bounce-back.
- **Governing law.** The law of the state of {{governing_state}} governs this agreement, without regard to conflict-of-law rules.
- **Counterparts and electronic signatures.** This agreement may be signed in counterparts and electronically. Each party consents to doing business electronically under the federal E-SIGN Act and the state's version of the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act (or New York's Electronic Signatures and Records Act). An electronic signature has the same effect as a handwritten one.

sections.title: Signatures
sections.body:
By signing below, each party agrees to this document.

**First party** — {{party_a_name}}

[[sig:partyA]]

Printed name: [[name:partyA]]
Title (if signing for a company): [[text:partyA:Title]]
Date: [[date:partyA]]

**Second party** — {{party_b_name}}

[[sig:partyB]]

Printed name: [[name:partyB]]
Title (if signing for a company): [[text:partyB:Title]]
Date: [[date:partyB]]

disclaimer: This is a starting template from the Chucksi open contract library. It is not legal advice, and using it does not create an attorney-client relationship. Laws vary by state and change over time. Have a licensed attorney in your state review it before you sign.
